sentences.text: Task 2. Iris is working on an online game for the next issue of the magazine.
There are three parts to Task 2.
In Part A, Iris explains the game to Dan.
In Part B, Dan plays the game.
In Part C, Dan and Iris discuss the game.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Part A. Fill in the missing information in the spaces provided in the Monster Maze Key.
Hey Iris. What are you working on?
Well, for this edition of the magazine, I’m designing some games.
You know so that our a subscribers can play them on their phone.
The idea is that they pay money to play and they can win money if they win.
Cool! What kind of games?
Well, the one I’m working on just now is called Monster Maze Have a look.
That’s the key.
I'm just finishing the example for the Key just now.
Hmm. The grid looks good.
OK, good. So where’s the entrance to the maze?
Is it at the top here?
No, the other way round.
The entrance to the maze is at the bottom where the numbers 1 to 6 are.
Ah I see, where the numbers are.
So the exit to the maze is at the top then.
Exactly. The exit at the top.
Oh, OK. Right.
And the grey squares must be walls or something.
Yes, that’s right, the grey squares are the walls of the maze.
And those circles, the Os.
That indicates the root you have taken through the maze.
Oh, I see the o's.
And what’s this M here?
That's the monster.
There are three but they're hidden when you play the game but when you land on one of the monsters an M appears and you lose a life.
Right. Still not sure if I get it.
So have a look at the example in the Key.
OK. Well, in the example, the player starts on A4, goes forward one square to B4, moves left one square to B3, moves forward three squares to E3
and then moves left one square and there at E2 he lands on the monster.
And is dead.
Yep. Yep. Eden alive.
Exactly.
Be. Plot Dan’s root by putting a circle in each square like the example shown above in the Monster Maze Key and put an M if he lands on a hidden monster.
So, do you want to play, Dan?
Sure. OK we can do it without the computer just now.
now. So I'll hide three monsters on the grid by writing down the grid number, and you have to go from the entrance of the maze and reach the exit without walking into the monsters.
You get two lives.
Sure. So this is my first life eh?
Yeah. Come on.
Go! OK, OK, I’m thinking.
I'll start on A4.
OK. You're fine.
Next move. I'll move forward one square then.
move right two squares.
gotcha You've landed on my monster.
ah Okay, so Your second life.
Right my second life.
Here goes. I'll start at a5 I move forward one square.
Now, I'll move left two squares.
OK. You're fine.
Move forward three squares.
And move right one square.
OK. Here it goes Move forward one square.
Did I make it?
Yes, well done Dan, you made it!
You survived the maze.
Hooray! I won.
No longer will I be We caught a loser!
Well, I don’t know about that!
Part C. Listen to Iris and Dan’s discussion and answer the questions.
Please note you do not have to answer in full sentences.
So, what do you think?
Any suggestions? Hmm.
Well, the grid’s a bit boring to look at.
You need to make the game look more colourful.
Yes, it does look a bit boring you're right.
I'll ask Gabby in graphics to make it more colourful.
And I'd suggest having more monsters.
that'll make it more challenging.
Yes, I suppose adding more monsters would make it more fun too.
But I have a question.
I was just wondering how will people actually play it online?
The game, I mean.
Well, we're going to allow two ways of playing the game.
The first one is by actually speaking, like we did.
Oh, that’s quite cool, so you speak to your smartphone and it marks your root on the grid.
Yes, that’s right.
All voice controlled.
The second way is that you can simply touch the screen.
Yes. I can imagine this working well with like touchscreen devices like smartphones.
But how can people be sure that the game’s not cheating and, you know, just placing the the monsters up to the player makes a move?
This is the tricky part.
It’s done in steps.
So in the first step, when the game starts, the game sends a document to the player’s phone.
OK, so what happens up to that?
Right, the second step is that when the game's over, a password appears on the screen, OK, right.
And then? What's the password for?
Right, so the third step is that the player opens the document with the password.
OK, cool. So they open the document in the third step.
Then the fourth and final step is that the player checks the location of the monsters.
OK, that is clever.
So when the player checks the location, he knows then that the game hasn’t been cheating.
Exactly.
